title: Personal book collection - browse the catalogue and manage my books

sourcesRead.contributes: user story, context (routes /books and /profile), accounts and data constraints, AC-1 to AC-12
base URL and JSON bodies, Bearer authentication and token endpoint, error envelope and error table, Book object fields, endpoints with bodies, statuses and errors

context: A signed-in reader browses and searches the Book Store catalogue on the Book Store page (/books) and keeps a personal collection of books, shown on the Profile page (/profile). Clients manage the collection through the Book Store API specified in the attached api-contract.md.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: `GET /BookStore/v1/Books` returns **200** with a `books` list; every entry carries all catalogue fields listed in the contract (isbn, title, subTitle, author, publish_date, publisher, pages, description, website).
acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /BookStore/v1/Books returns 200 with a books list; every entry carries all catalogue fields listed in the contract (isbn, title, subTitle, author, publish_date, publisher, pages, description, website).
outcomes: the body has a `books` list
every entry carries isbn, title, subTitle, author, publish_date, publisher, pages, description and website

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Looking up one book with `GET /BookStore/v1/Book?ISBN=<isbn>` returns **200** with the same data as that book's entry in the catalogue.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Looking up one book with GET /BookStore/v1/Book?ISBN=<isbn> returns 200 with the same data as that book's entry in the catalogue.
outcomes: the returned book has the same data as that book's entry in GET /BookStore/v1/Books

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The Book Store page `/books` lists every book returned by the catalogue API, each with its title, author and publisher.
acceptanceCriteria.text: The Book Store page /books lists every book returned by the catalogue API, each with its title, author and publisher.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The search box on `/books` (placeholder "Type to search") filters the list while typing, case-insensitively, on title, author or publisher. Examples: "javascript" shows exactly Learning JavaScript Design Patterns, Speaking JavaScript, Programming JavaScript Applications and Eloquent JavaScript, Second Edition; "zakas" shows only Understanding ECMAScript 6; "No Starch" shows only Eloquent JavaScript, Second Edition and Understanding ECMAScript 6. A term that matches no book leaves no book rows in the list.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Adding a book that is already in the user's collection is rejected with the "already present" error from the contract; the collection still contains that book exactly once.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Adding a book that is already in the user's collection is rejected with the "already present" error from the contract; the collection still contains that book exactly once.
outcomes: adding the book again is rejected with the E4 error: 400, code 1210, message "ISBN already present in the User's Collection!"
the collection still contains that book exactly once

acceptanceCriteria.quote: On the Profile page, deleting one book (the row's delete icon, then confirming "Do you want to delete this book?" with OK) removes that row only; the other books remain. Afterwards the user's collection in the API no longer contains the deleted book and still contains the others.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Collection calls without a valid token are refused with the "not authorized" error from the contract: adding, deleting and reading a user's collection without a token, and reading or adding to another user's collection with one's own token.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Collection calls without a valid token are refused with the "not authorized" error from the contract: adding, deleting and reading a user's collection without a token, and reading or adding to another user's collection with one's own token.
outcomes: adding (POST /BookStore/v1/Books) without a token is refused with the E1 error: 401, code 1200, message "User not authorized!"
deleting (DELETE /BookStore/v1/Book) without a token is refused with the E1 error: 401, code 1200, message "User not authorized!"
reading a user's collection (GET /Account/v1/User/{UUID}) without a token is refused with the E1 error: 401, code 1200, message "User not authorized!"
reading another user's collection (GET /Account/v1/User/{UUID}) with one's own token is refused with the E1 error: 401, code 1200, message "User not authorized!"
adding to another user's collection (POST /BookStore/v1/Books with the other user's userId) with one's own token is refused with the E1 error: 401, code 1200, message "User not authorized!"

endpoints.request: JSON body { "userName": "...", "password": "..." } with Content-Type: application/json (api-contract.md#L3, #L9); obtains the Bearer token (story.md#L31)
JSON body { "userId": "<UUID>", "collectionOfIsbns": [ { "isbn": "..." }, ... ] } with Content-Type: application/json and Authorization: Bearer <token>

endpoints.success: 204, empty body - removes all books of the user
endpoints.request: ?UserId=<UUID>, with Authorization: Bearer <token>; used to leave each used collection empty (story.md#L30)

rules.text: A Book object has the fields isbn (string), title (string), subTitle (string), author (string), publish_date (string, ISO-8601), publisher (string), pages (number), description (string) and website (string, URL).

errorModel.case: Not authorized: a protected call with no or an invalid token (POST /BookStore/v1/Books, DELETE /BookStore/v1/Book, GET /Account/v1/User/{UUID}), or with another user's userId (POST /BookStore/v1/Books) or UUID (GET /Account/v1/User/{UUID})
ISBN not in catalogue: GET /BookStore/v1/Book with an unknown ISBN, or POST /BookStore/v1/Books with an unknown ISBN
errorModel.body: { "code": "1205", "message": "ISBN supplied is not available in Books Collection!" }

errorModel.case: ISBN not in user's collection: DELETE /BookStore/v1/Book for an ISBN that is not in the user's collection
errorModel.body: { "code": "1206", "message": "ISBN supplied is not available in User's Collection!" }

errorModel.case: ISBN already in user's collection: POST /BookStore/v1/Books with an ISBN already in the collection
errorModel.body: { "code": "1210", "message": "ISBN already present in the User's Collection!" }

auth.mechanism: Protected calls send Authorization: Bearer <token>; the token is obtained with POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken, body { "userName": "...", "password": "..." }
auth.credentials: the QA team's pre-provisioned test users; user names and passwords are kept in the team's secret store, never in the test code

testData.strategy: Tests use the QA team's pre-provisioned test users (credentials from the team's secret store); user creation is switched off, so no user is created or deleted. Books come from the standard catalogue.
constraints: User creation is switched off in the QA environment; do not create or delete users (story.md#L29)
The test users are shared by every run (story.md#L30)
Catalogue books used in the examples: 9781449325862 "Git Pocket Guide", 9781593277574 "Understanding ECMAScript 6", 9781449331818 "Learning JavaScript Design Patterns" (story.md#L32)
testData.cleanup: Each test leaves the collection of every user it used empty (story.md#L30); DELETE /BookStore/v1/Books?UserId={UUID} removes all books of the user (api-contract.md#L58)

outOfScope: Creating users (POST /Account/v1/User): user creation is switched off; tests must not create users (story.md#L29, api-contract.md#L12)
Deleting users (DELETE /Account/v1/User/{UUID}): tests must not delete users (story.md#L29, api-contract.md#L13)
